messages:
Aisha: sharing a concise onboarding + account-health runbook that we can hand to SEs and CSMs. Focus: caching, batching, streaming, plus a quick renewal-risk pulse and feedback capture template. can you skim?
Marco: thanks — will review. do you want this to be customer-facing copy or internal playbook?
Aisha: both — one doc for customer-facing "quick runbook" and one internal checklist with escalation triggers. I'll paste the customer-facing draft below. keep it short.
Aisha: CUSTOMER-FACING RUNBOOK (short):
- Goal: Get model response latency <350ms p50 for interactive flows; reduce token cost via prefix caching and batching.
- Quick milestones: 1) Prod keys, 2) Test calls (10-100 reqs/min), 3) Enable streaming for UX, 4) Verify KV-prefetch, 5) Go-live + 72h watch.
- Basic health checks (run before handoff): 
  1) Connectivity: `curl -sS https://api.redwood.example/v1/health | jq .status` -> expect `ok`
  2) Latency sample: run 50 short-gen calls (stream=false) and record p50/p95
  3) Errors: check gateway 5xx rate <1% and client 4xx flagging
- Streaming quickstart (enable for chat-like UX):
  - Minimal request: `curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","stream":true,"input":"hi"}'`
  - Fallback: if `stream` connection times out >10s repeatedly, toggle `stream=false` until region/Dedicated capacity available.
- Caching & batching tips (customer-facing):
  - Cache common prefixes (system prompts, product spec snippets) on our side to reduce tokens.
  - Use short batch windows (50–150ms) for throughput without harming latency.
- If you see sudden usage drop >40% or sustained error rate >2% for 30+ minutes -> flag CSM/SE.

Marco: this reads great. internal checklist?
Aisha: INTERNAL CHECKLIST (one-page):
1) Preflight (SE): verify API keys, region routing, model variant pinned.
2) Smoke (CS): 10 warmup calls, confirm token billing matches expected.
3) Performance (Eng/SE): run 5k simulated requests with TTL distribution used by customer (script below).
4) Streaming stress test: open 200 concurrent streams at target QPS and monitor agent memory/conn counts.
5) Fallback policy: configure route priority -> primary dedicated pool, secondary hosted fallback, third lower-capacity model.
6) Renewal-risk flags to note in CRM: usage decline >30% MoM, repeated quality regressions, feature blockers for 2+ weeks.

Aisha: Simulated request script (basic):
```
# simulate 5000 requests at ramp
seq 1 5000 | xargs -n1 -P50 -I{} curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","input":"test","stream":false}' >/dev/null
```

Samir: add a short feedback capture template so CSMs can collect quantifiable signals before renewals.

Aisha: FEEDBACK PULSE EMAIL (one-paragraph + 3-question form):
Subject: Quick pulse — how is Redwood inference working for you?
Hi {{Name}},
We want to make sure inference performance is meeting your needs. Could you spare 2 minutes for 3 quick items?
1) Satisfaction with latency & uptime (1-5): __
2) Anything blocking you from using streaming / lower-cost models? (yes/no + short)
3) Biggest pain right now (free text)
Thanks — we use this to prioritize rollouts and support.

Marco: maybe include a tiny NPS and usage ask.
Aisha: added on the doc. also included a short troubleshooting snippet for streaming flaps: check client-side keepalive, server timeout logs, and if you see `RST` at ~15s for many clients -> suspect LB idle timeout.

Elena: will turn into a 1-pager and a shared Google doc for customers. want me to own the customer copy?
Aisha: yes please, assign to Elena. cc @Samir for renewal flags.

cs-bot: reminder set — follow-up with customer 5 days after go-live (task created: CS-1457).

Samir: ship it to Acme on Monday. small ask: add one line about expected billing impact from caching (eg ~20–40% token reduction typical).

Aisha: good call — added. I'll post the final customer-facing doc here tomorrow and link the internal checklist in SF. thanks all :thumbsup:
